properties.statement: [BL-201] Requirement.concern is an eleven-value ility axis that NO CODE READS — the quality axis was designed twice and the first one was never wired up
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Same census, 2026-08-04.* Requirement.concern \u2014 core / logistics / sustainment / safety / security / cost / schedule / manufacturability / usability / environmental / other, indexed, present since the beginning, described in the schema as covering *\"the ILS considerations an SME surfaces\"* \u2014 is core on all 110 requirements, and grep '\"concern\"' crates/reflow2-core/src/*.rs returns nothing. Meanwhile v0.23.0 shipped ility_report ([BL-184]), which computes nine quality axes by mapping existing findings onto them \u2014 and correctly reports performance/security/scalability/observability as NOT INFORMED, because nothing computes over them. The field that would let a user DECLARE those concerns has been sitting on Requirement the whole time. So: either wire concern into ility_report as declared (as opposed to computed) evidence for an axis \u2014 carefully, since [BL-184]'s load-bearing rule is that adverse is INHERITED and never re-judged, and a declared concern is not a finding \u2014 or retire the property under retire-from-design and stop advertising it through describe_schema. Deciding which IS the row. Size S", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-201 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S."}
